- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (0.00) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for lagged momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or negative — apply +1.5% bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits persistent underestimation; apply +2% bias to all forecasts unless sentiment turns positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late period (last 7–10 days) — reduce forecast by 1–3% in final 7 days if sentiment is flat or negative.
